set_aside.subject: purity of admitted function implementations
set_aside.text: “A flow is a small proven graph of two kinds of node: a pure function an agent wrote” and “Functions are pure” versus “the kernel neither checks that nor masks any other fact of the process”
set_aside.question: Can an implementation whose output depends on an undeclared process fact be admitted and run as a function node, and if so in what sense is the node proven pure?
options: Such an implementation may be admitted and remains a valid function node because purity is only an assumption about authored code.
Such an implementation is invalid, requiring some specified evidence or enforcement before admission.
Admission may rely only on observed trial outputs, so an implementation is treated as pure until contrary output is observed.
set_aside.default_guess: Treat purity as an unenforced author obligation and admit according to the existing corpus and contract checks.

witness.initial: A contract has a nonempty corpus, and an implementation reads an unmasked process fact while producing schema-valid output.
events: The kernel runs every trial while the process fact has value A, and all cases pass.
The kernel admits and activates the implementation.
outcomes: The implementation is a valid admitted pure function because admission judges only observed outputs.
The implementation must be refused or its proof cannot be issued because it is not input-dependent.
The agent and anyone inspecting the admission or running the flow sees the difference.
witness.observer: The agent and owner inspecting the verdict or attempting to run the flow

set_aside.subject: repeatability violation during a real execution
set_aside.text: “Every promise in these documents that a function repeats itself — equal outputs on equal inputs, a repaired slot staying repaired, a verdict that holds — is a promise about code whose outputs depend only on its inputs; the kernel neither checks that”
set_aside.question: What observable result and record are required when an admitted implementation later produces a different, schema-valid output for an input previously exercised by the same pinned implementation?
options: Accept the new output as a successful execution because the kernel performs no repeatability check.
Fail the node as a purity or verdict violation.
Accept the output but invalidate the admission or activation for later runs.
The repeatability promise is purely conditional and imposes no runtime behavior when its premise is false.
set_aside.default_guess: Accept the schema-valid output and leave the admission and activation unchanged, treating the promise as conditional.

witness.initial: One implementation is admitted and active; a trial case with input X produced output Y.
events: An owner or agent runs a flow pinning that implementation with input X.
The implementation observes an unmasked process fact and returns different schema-valid output Z.
outcomes: The node succeeds with Z and the admission remains valid because no dependency check is made.
The node fails or the verdict is invalidated because equal inputs were promised equal outputs.
witness.observer: The run initiator and later inspectors of the run, trace, verdict and activation

set_aside.subject: meaning of a function's inputs for determinism
set_aside.text: “code whose outputs depend only on its inputs”
set_aside.question: Which facts count as “its inputs” for this promise: only declared input-port values, or also the pinned implementation, contract, sandbox configuration, resource limits, interpreter/runtime version, and other execution context?
options: Only values supplied through declared input ports count.
Declared input values plus the pinned implementation and contract count.
All execution context visible to the code counts, making visible process facts inputs for this statement.
A specific enumerated subset of execution context counts.
set_aside.default_guess: Use declared port values together with the pinned implementation and contract; treat all other observable process facts as undeclared dependencies.

witness.initial: The same admitted implementation receives the same declared value X before and after the installation changes Python runtime version; both executions satisfy the contract schema.
events: An agent runs the function before the runtime change and it returns Y.
The installation changes the runtime version.
An agent runs the same pinned implementation with X and it returns Z because standard-library behavior differs.
outcomes: The repeatability promise is broken because runtime version is not an input.
Both executions satisfy the promise because execution context is included among the inputs.
witness.observer: The agents or owner comparing the two traces and outputs

set_aside.subject: process facts visible to untrusted function code
set_aside.text: “the kernel neither checks that nor masks any other fact of the process”
set_aside.question: What process facts may an untrusted function observe, and how is this statement reconciled with the promises of “no secret,” “no filesystem beyond its input,” disposable isolation, and bounded resources?
options: Only facts not otherwise prohibited, such as process ID, runtime version, locale, environment shape and resource state, remain visible.
Every process fact is potentially visible except credentials explicitly filtered elsewhere.
The sandbox must specify an allowlist of visible process facts.
The phrase describes nondeterminism only and does not alter the sandbox visibility boundary.
set_aside.default_guess: Read “other fact” as only non-secret sandbox metadata and state not prohibited elsewhere, but the permitted set remains unspecified.

witness.initial: A function uses a standard-library call not named as blocked to read an environment value or other sandbox process metadata.
events: The trial executes successfully and returns a schema-valid value derived from that metadata.
outcomes: The access is allowed because the kernel expressly does not mask other process facts.
The execution is a sandbox violation because function code may receive only its declared input and no secret or unrelated process state.
witness.observer: The submitting agent through the trial result and sandbox-failure record
